author: Inside Edition
description: Inmates at the Franklin County Corrections Center in Ohio are using their artistic talents to help shelter pups get adopted. The convicts have drawn portraits of the dogs, and shelters are displaying the artworks on their kennels. The illustrations are so impressive, people stop to take notice. And that helps the previously overlooked pups find new homes. So far, 20 dogs have had their portraits drawn, and 18 have been adopted. Inside Edition Digital's Andrea Swindall has more.
title: Inmates' Artwork Helps Shelter Dogs Find Forever Homes
